rv.q: Ms. Midler gives the most lusciously entertaining performance of the Broadway season.
To put it more pithily: the casting of Bette Midler as Sue Mengers is genius.
Midler's consummate ability to deliver brassy chutzpah, fierceness and silky comic seduction at the same time is harnessed to perfection, allowing just a judicious whisper of vulnerability.
Which, despite the expert attention of director Joe Mantello, is what I’ll Eat You Last would do without Midler.
You might find such characters and events indulgent, insufferable, trivial, even preening
“I’ll Eat You Last” is wickedly entertaining precisely because performer and material are so perfectly matched.
But the play itself feels more like an extended celebrity impression than a fully realized theatrical experience.
Midler manages a fabulous feat: She marshals all her own famously divine Bette-ness to bring to life a kindred spirit.
Midler reminds us what a strong dramatic actress she can be, whether evoking Mengers' challenges or showing us the moxie that got her through them.
As the monologue grows in texture, Midler shines, serving less of a caricature and more of a person--someone who it turns out has some real feeling lurking beneath the caftan and the zingers.
But Midler is delicious and worth crossing the playground to get a ticket.
But in light of this rare opportunity to catch Midler onstage, a more substantial meal would have been nice instead of 90 minutes of pure dessert.
Thanks to the lazy writing and acting, Mengers goes missing.
Those who come knowing Midler but not Mengers (who died in 2011) will be disappointed by this weightless valedictory, for there’s no swan, and no song.
